picks.rationale: She is BRCA1-mutant and treatment-naive, and talazoparib is the highest-trapping PARP inhibitor with an ORR of 62.6% and PFS HR 0.54 in EMBRACA. The upside I am chasing: a deep single-agent response that shrinks the solitary liver lesion enough to make ablation or resection a curative-intent move, all without committing her to a cytotoxic backbone yet. This is a real drug I can start now, not a trial slot she has to wait for. The germline-vs-somatic question is unresolved, but somatic BRCA1 is still PARP-actionable, and the Stanford somatic-talazoparib trial (NCT03990896) already shows ~38% ORR, so I do not treat that ambiguity as a stop sign.
primary_concerns: Grade 3+ anemia runs about 39% in EMBRACA; she will likely need dose holds or transfusion support
EMBRACA OS was not significantly improved (HR 0.76), so the PFS win may not convert to survival
If BRCA1 is somatic-only the FDA breast label technically requires germline, which could create a payer fight

picks.rationale: The PETRA breast subset at 60 mg gave an ORR of 48.4% (95% CI 35.7-61.3) with mPFS 9.1 mo and markedly less hematologic toxicity than olaparib or talazoparib, which is exactly the profile I want when the goal is durable disease control in a fit 42-year-old. PARP1-selectivity is the mechanistic bet: spare PARP2, keep the synthetic-lethal kill on her BRCA1-null tumor, and buy a wider therapeutic window so she can stay on drug longer. I will be honest that the breast subset mixed HR+ and TNBC and this is conference-abstract data, not a peer-reviewed TNBC-specific readout. Even so, a ~48% ORR in a BRCA-driven population is a signal I am not willing to leave on the table, and HS-10502 gives the same class a second shot on goal.
primary_concerns: No published paper and no per-term grade 3+ table yet, so the tolerability claim rests on an abstract
Breast cohort pooled HR+ and TNBC, so the TNBC-specific ORR could be lower
Enrollment is 2L+ with prior-therapy expectation, so she likely needs a first line before she qualifies

picks.rationale: TOPACIO hit a 47% ORR in the BRCA-mutant TNBC subgroup with a chemo-free regimen, and this patient is the canonical responder: BRCA1-mutant, 3+ stromal TILs, TMB 14. The preclinical APOBEC/immune work says a TMB-high TIL-rich tumor is primed for PD-1 blockade, so I am stacking a PARP inhibitor that generates neoantigens onto a checkpoint that exploits them. The MEDIOLA cohort (63% ORR, DCR 80%) points the same direction with a PARP + PD-L1 pair. It is a small single-arm signal and niraparib is off-label in breast, but the biology here is clean and the ceiling is high.
primary_concerns: n=15 in the BRCA-mut TOPACIO subgroup, so the 47% could regress toward the mean in a larger cohort
Niraparib is not labeled in breast cancer, which invites payer denial versus labeled olaparib/talazoparib
Overlapping anemia/thrombocytopenia plus immune-related AEs, and a B2M/HLA-loss subclone would blunt the ICI half

picks.rationale: If her pending PD-L1 CPS returns >=10, KEYNOTE-355 is the one regimen here with a proven 1L survival benefit: OS HR 0.73, median 23.0 vs 16.1 months. Pair the checkpoint with a gemcitabine/carboplatin backbone and I get the platinum her BRCA1 tumor is doubly sensitive to (TNT: 68% vs 33% ORR in BRCA-mut) plus the immune signal her TIL-3+/TMB-14 phenotype predicts. This is my highest-floor pick, which is why it is not rank 1 for me, but the combined efficacy is hard to argue with. The whole plan hinges on the CPS result; below 10 the labeled benefit evaporates and I would pivot to a TROP2-ADC or PARP strategy.
primary_concerns: PD-L1 CPS is pending and gates the entire regimen; CPS <10 removes the labeled benefit
Benefit is anchored on CPS, not TMB or TILs, so her favorable phenotype does not rescue a CPS-low result
Grade 3+ AE rate ~68% from the chemo backbone, heavier than the chemo-free PARP options above

picks.rationale: POLθ inhibition is synthetic-lethal with HR deficiency the same way PARP inhibition is, so ART6043 rides her BRCA1 loss, and the olaparib-combination arm is where the early activity showed up (1 confirmed PR plus 1 unconfirmed CR across 42 patients). It earned FDA Fast Track in Feb 2026 for gBRCA HER2-negative breast and has a randomized phase 2 running, which makes it the most advanced POLθ program on her axis. This is a genuinely thin signal in a heavily pretreated cohort, and I am ranking it as a forward-looking option for when she progresses, not a 1L move. The reason it stays on my list: POLθ has a plausible answer to PARP resistance, and I want that card in hand before she needs it.
primary_concerns: Two responses across 42 combination patients is a whisper of a signal, not proof of efficacy
Median 4 prior therapies in the reported cohort; activity in a fitter earlier-line patient is unproven
No peer-reviewed data or per-term safety table, and a washout requirement puts it well past 1L

picks.rationale: CX-5461 is the one agent in the dossier that hits both of her drivers at once: HRD synthetic lethality plus MYC-dependent rDNA transcription, and her tumor is MYC-amplified on top of BRCA1-mutant. The IND.231 responses clustered in BRCA/PALB2 breast carriers, which is the direction I want even though the confirmed responders were BRCA2 and PALB2 rather than BRCA1. I am putting it last on purpose: the ORR was 14%, phototoxicity was dose-limiting, and a 2023 paper flagged it as a nonselective mutagen, which is a real problem for anyone I am framing as potentially curative. It stays on the list only as a late-line dual-mechanism shot if the cleaner DDR options are exhausted.
primary_concerns: BRCA1-specific benefit is inferred; the actual responders were BRCA2/PALB2
Mutagenicity signal is disqualifying if any curative-intent or long-survival framing is in play
Grade 3-4 phototoxicity in 15% and a demanding IV schedule for modest 14% ORR

notes: I deliberately weighted the BRCA1/DDR axis over the more conventional 1L chemo-immunotherapy default because this is where the striking effect sizes live for her genotype, and because a deep PARP response is the most plausible route to converting a solitary liver lesion into a curative-intent local-therapy candidate. I left capivasertib off entirely: CAPItello-290 was flatly negative in TNBC including the PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-altered stratum (OS HR 1.05), and EPIK-B3 alpelisib was terminated, so the PI3K/AKT axis has no upside story worth championing here even with her PIK3CA-mut + PTEN-loss. The mutant-selective PI3Kα agents (RLY-2608, tersolisib) are HR+ cross-subtype precedent only, so I parked them. No toxicity_vetoes are set and efficacy weight is 0.7, which is what licenses the aggressive DDR-forward ranking.

picks.intervention_label: Pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w + carboplatin AUC2 / gemcitabine 1000 mg/m^2 d1,8 q21d (KEYNOTE-355 backbone)
picks.rationale: This is the 1L regimen with the longest confirmatory follow-up in metastatic TNBC: KEYNOTE-355 read out final OS at 44-month median follow-up (mOS 23.0 vs 16.1 mo, HR 0.73), so I am not extrapolating from an interim signal. The G3+ AE rate was 68.1% vs 66.9% for chemo alone, meaning pembrolizumab adds little incremental high-grade toxicity over the backbone the patient would receive anyway, and the immune-mediated G3+ events (5.3%) map onto the well-codified irAE algorithm every treating center already runs. The TIL-3+/TMB-14 phenotype is the subgroup that benefits most, which reinforces the choice without my having to lean on off-label TMB extrapolation. One hard gate: the regimen requires PD-L1 CPS >=10 by 22C3, and CPS is pending. Confidence is high on the regimen but conditional on that assay returning >=10; if CPS <10 this drops out and rank 3 leads.
primary_concerns: PD-L1 CPS is pending; the entire pick is contingent on 22C3 CPS >=10 returning, and roughly 20-30% of primary-vs-liver-met pairs are discordant, so score the breast primary block.

Adds pembrolizumab irAE risk (G3+ immune-mediated 5.3%) on top of the chemo backbone — manageable with the standard algorithm, but a B2M/HLA class I check is cheap insurance against primary ICI resistance in an MSS tumor.

picks.intervention_label: Olaparib 300 mg PO BID (OlympiAD, BRCA1-directed PARP inhibitor)
picks.rationale: Among the BRCA1-directed options this has the maturest safety record and the most predictable toxicity of any oral agent on the list. OlympiAD reported G3+ AEs at 36.6% (vs 50.5% for chemo), discontinuation at 4.9%, with anemia as the single dominant grade-3 event at 16.1% and a management pathway (dose hold, transfusion, growth-factor support) that oncology teams run in their sleep. The OlympiA adjuvant dataset (n=1836) extends the safety window and, importantly, showed no MDS/AML excess over placebo at the 300 mg BID dose, which matters for a 42-year-old who may live years on or after this drug. Eligibility gates on the germline-vs-somatic call: FDA labeling in breast is germline-restricted, so I want the germline BRCA1 result before writing it. If the variant reads somatic-only, olaparib becomes off-label and I would defer to the platinum backbone rather than an off-label PARP write.
primary_concerns: Germline-vs-somatic status is unresolved; the labeled breast indication is germline-only, so a somatic-only BRCA1 call moves this to off-label and I would not lead with it.
Anemia (G3+ 16.1%) is the expected dominant AE — check baseline CBC and iron studies and set a transfusion/hold threshold before starting, but this is a characterized, low-surprise toxicity.

picks.intervention_label: Carboplatin AUC2 + gemcitabine 1000 mg/m^2 d1,8 q21d (PD-L1-agnostic, germline-agnostic 1L backbone in BRCA1-mut TNBC)
picks.rationale: This is my no-biomarker-needed fallback and the reason it sits at rank 3 rather than lower: it works regardless of how the PD-L1 CPS and germline BRCA1 questions resolve, so it is the one option that cannot be gated out from under the patient. The BRCA1 platinum-sensitivity evidence is direct — in TNT the BRCA-mut subgroup had an ORR of 68.0% on carboplatin vs 33.3% on docetaxel (interaction p=0.01, mPFS HR 0.44) — and carboplatin's myelosuppression is as predictable and management-algorithmed as any cytotoxic we use. As single-agent carboplatin in TNT the G3+ neutropenia was 12% and thrombocytopenia 7%, lower than the combination regimens; adding gemcitabine raises the count but keeps the AE profile inside familiar, dose-modifiable territory. It also doubles as the induction backbone if the board later wants an olaparib or ICI maintenance strategy.
primary_concerns: Additive myelosuppression from the carbo/gem doublet — day-8 counts drive frequent dose modification; predictable but demands proactive CBC monitoring and a growth-factor plan.
A cytotoxic doublet gives up the OS advantage that the pembrolizumab arm carries if CPS >=10 returns, so this should stay a fallback rather than the default unless the biomarker gates close it off.

picks.intervention_label: Talazoparib 1 mg PO daily (EMBRACA, alternate BRCA1-directed PARP inhibitor)
picks.rationale: Talazoparib is the equally-labeled alternative to olaparib and I rank it just below rather than beside it purely on the hematologic-tolerability delta. EMBRACA is a mature registrational RCT (PFS HR 0.54, mPFS 8.6 vs 5.6 mo), so the efficacy is not in question. The reason it is rank 4 and not rank 2 is the AE-grade distribution: G3+ anemia ~39%, neutropenia ~21%, thrombocytopenia ~15% — a substantially heavier hematologic burden than olaparib's 16.1% anemia at comparable PFS. For a patient who may also need myelosuppressive chemo before or after, I prefer the PARP inhibitor that spends less marrow reserve. Same germline gate as olaparib applies. If the patient has a specific reason to favor once-daily dosing or tolerates anemia well, it moves up; otherwise olaparib is the cleaner first PARP choice.
primary_concerns: Higher-grade hematologic toxicity than olaparib at similar efficacy (G3+ anemia ~39%, thrombocytopenia ~15%) — the deciding factor for ranking it below olaparib rather than beside it.
Germline-restricted label, same as olaparib; a somatic-only BRCA1 call makes this off-label too.

picks.intervention_label: Sacituzumab govitecan 10 mg/kg IV d1,8 q21d — held in reserve for 2L per ASCENT label
picks.rationale: I am ranking this fifth deliberately as the pre-committed next line, not as a 1L candidate. ASCENT is a mature phase-3 dataset (final OS HR 0.51, mOS 11.8 vs 6.9 mo) with a fully-characterized toxicity signature — G3+ neutropenia ~51%, diarrhea 10%, febrile neutropenia 6% — and, critically, the FDA label restricts it to >=2 prior lines including a taxane, so the patient is not eligible now. Naming it here documents the safest, best-evidenced downstream option so the 1L choice is made knowing the fallback is a labeled ADC with a known SN-38 AE algorithm rather than something experimental. The neutropenia rate is high but predictable and G-CSF-manageable, which is exactly the kind of characterized toxicity I want holding the 2L slot.
primary_concerns: Not enrollable in 1L — the ASCENT label requires >=2 prior lines including a taxane, so this is a reserved next-line option, not a current pick.
G3+ neutropenia ~51% and febrile neutropenia 6% require upfront G-CSF planning, but the AE profile is fully characterized with an established management pathway.

notes: Posture on this re-run: the 14 new gate-swept trials and the refreshed evidence do not move my top of the order, and in a couple of places they harden my priors. CAPItello-290 is now published negative (OS HR 0.92 ITT, 1.05 in the AKT-altered stratum the patient sits in), so capivasertib is off my 1L list despite the PIK3CA/PTEN fit. VIOLETTE plus the plasmaMATCH Cohort E readout confirm the ATR/PARP combinations are additively myelosuppressive (anemia and thrombocytopenia both up) without beating olaparib alone, and the adavosertib WEE1 arm closed for toxicity — so I am not ranking any DDR-combination in 1L. The new POLtheta programs (ART6043, novobiocin, SYN818), the PARP1-selective agents (saruparib/HS-10502), the PARG agents (IDE161/DAT-2645), and CX-5461 are all phase-1 or abstract-level with no per-term G3+ tables released; CX-5461 additionally carries a phototoxicity DLT (G3-4 15%, any-grade 60%) and a published mutagenicity flag, which for a treatment-naive, potentially long-lived 42-year-old is exactly the uncharacterized long-tail risk my prior deprioritizes. I have left them out of the ranked five and named the specific missing safety datum rather than downgrading them for novelty alone. preferences.json carries no toxicity_vetoes, so I hold no round-1 veto here; my round-2 job is to watch for any co-panelist 1L pick that leans on those early-phase DDR agents without a compensating safety-mitigation argument.

picks.rationale: Nothing in the 14 new trials or the DDR evidence tier displaces this. Two independent registrational phase 3 trials sit under PARP inhibition in germline BRCA1/2 HER2-negative mBC: OlympiAD (n=302, PFS HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.43-0.80) and EMBRACA (n=431, PFS HR 0.54, 95% CI 0.41-0.71). Both pre-registered, both a registered primary-endpoint hit at conventional alpha, both low RoB 2 with BICR-adjudicated PFS, both replicating the synthetic-lethality preclinical anchor. That is the whole evidence bar the persona exists to defend, and the new saruparib/HS-10502 PARP1-selective abstracts don't clear it. Saruparib's 48.4% breast ORR (PETRA, n=31 at 60 mg) reads well, but it is an AACR conference abstract with a mixed HR+/TNBC subset, no per-term AE table, and a null PMID. Do not let a next-generation single-arm ORR outrank a replicated RCT for the same axis. The gating step is unchanged: germline-vs-somatic BRCA1. Somatic-only collapses olaparib to off-label in breast, and the somatic-talazoparib expansion (NCT03990896) is still a single-arm 1L-3L cohort, not a phase 3 substitute.
primary_concerns: RoB 2, deviations from intended interventions: both trials open-label. I accept it because the PFS primary is BICR-adjudicated, but it goes in the ledger.
Germline-vs-somatic BRCA1 is still unresolved on tumor NGS and it gates the breast label. The somatic-talazoparib row (NCT03990896) is single-arm, ORR-only, not a randomized readout.
Cumulative MDS/AML risk runs 1-2% across the pooled registrational PARP dataset; serial CBC monitoring is mandatory over a 12-18 month horizon.

picks.rationale: Phase 3, n=847, pre-specified primary PFS in the CPS>=10 stratum at HR 0.65 (95% CI 0.49-0.86, p=0.0012), with a confirmed OS gain at final readout (median +7 mo). RoB 2 low across domains. The label tracks the biomarker rather than the mechanism, which is exactly why I trust it: the CPS<10 subset showed no benefit and the indication respected that. TMB 14 mut/Mb and 3+ TILs are real features of this tumor, but KEYNOTE-355 was not powered on either, so they cannot substitute for the CPS gate. The new ASCENT-04 SG+pembrolizumab 1L row (n=443) points at the same CPS>=10 population but is a 2025 presentation still in press with no published primary I can risk-of-bias; I am not ranking a regimen on a slide deck.
primary_concerns: Eligibility is entirely gated on 22C3 CPS>=10, which is pending. CPS<10 closes the regimen and the patient does not inherit benefit from TMB-14 or 3+ TILs; that is unsanctioned biomarker extrapolation.

The KEYNOTE-158 TMB-H basket (n=102, single-arm, ORR 29%) cannot bridge a CPS<10 gap in 1L treatment-naive disease. It is 2L+ label, no comparator, and breast was not in the original basket, so the 29% is uninterpretable here.
RoB 2: low across allocation, blinding, missing-data, measurement, selective-reporting. Sponsor-run analysis noted, not de-rated; KEYNOTE-522 replicates direction of effect in a different setting.

picks.rationale: The second independent phase 3 anchor in the same indication: n=431, PFS HR 0.54 (95% CI 0.41-0.71), p<0.001, low RoB 2. Two sponsors, two molecules, one gating biomarker, replicated direction and magnitude. That mutual replication is what I want to see before I credit an axis, and it is why the PARP RCTs sit above every new DDR agent in the dossier regardless of how clean the mechanism looks on a poster. Ranks below olaparib on tolerability alone: grade >=3 anemia 39% on talazoparib versus 16.1% on olaparib. Evidence quality is at parity with pick 1.
primary_concerns: Same germline BRCA1 gating as pick 1.
Grade >=3 anemia 39% compresses deliverable dose intensity; a tolerability concern, not an evidence-quality one.
Same open-label RoB 2 caveat; BICR-adjudicated PFS is the mitigation.

picks.intervention_label: Olaparib + ceralasertib (ATR-i) — plasmaMATCH Cohort E, later-line only
picks.rationale: This is the best-evidenced of the new DDR entries, and I want to be precise about how far that gets it. plasmaMATCH Cohort E is published (PMID 37773077, ROBINS-I moderate, tier 2b), TNBC-specific, n=70, ORR 17.1% (95% CI 10.4-25.5), with responses in HRR-wildtype and functional-HRD tumors that fit her BRCA1 + TP53 replication-stress phenotype. That beats the rest of the new axis on maturity: it is a real published cohort, not the ART6043 ESMO 2025 press summary (n=61, 1 confirmed PR across 42 combination patients, no AE table, null PMID) and not the abstract-only POLθ/PARG/PARP1-selective rows. But it is a single-arm phase 2 with a surrogate endpoint, and the dedicated randomized test of this exact concept, VIOLETTE, failed to beat olaparib monotherapy. A 17% ORR with a 4.3-month median PFS in a pretreated 2L+ cohort is not a 1L treatment-naive readout, and this patient is treatment-naive de novo M1. I rank it here as a later-line, trial-enrollment option, not as a substitute for the PARP monotherapy she is actually eligible for now.
primary_concerns: Single-arm phase 2, ORR surrogate, no comparator. The one randomized test of PARP+ATR in this setting (VIOLETTE) did not beat olaparib alone, so the combination's incremental value over PARP monotherapy is unproven.
Setting mismatch: Cohort E is 2L+ pretreated mTNBC; this patient is 1L treatment-naive. The 17% ORR does not transfer to the front line, and washout requirements make it non-1L-enrollable.

The paired CX-5461 citation (IND.231, PMID 35750695, ORR 14%, ROBINS-I moderate) is genuinely published but its responders cluster in BRCA2/PALB2 carriers, so BRCA1 benefit is inferred, not shown; grade 3-4 phototoxicity in 15% is a chemotype liability separate from the DDR mechanism.

picks.intervention_label: Carboplatin AUC2 + gemcitabine 1000 mg/m^2 d1,8 q21d (PD-L1-low BRCA1-mut fallback)
picks.rationale: If CPS returns <10 and pembrolizumab closes, the BRCA1-directed platinum doublet is the defensible PD-L1-agnostic backbone, and I will be straight that the evidence here is thinner than picks 1-3. TNT (n=376) found no overall PFS difference between carboplatin and docetaxel, but the pre-specified BRCA-mutated subgroup (n=43) showed PFS HR 0.59 (95% CI 0.36-0.97, p=0.04) favoring carboplatin, with roughly double the ORR (68% vs 33%). n=43 is a small subgroup with a wide CI. This is class evidence plus three decades of carboplatin/gemcitabine post-marketing experience, not a registrational 1L anchor, and I rank it last precisely because it is the least-bad supported option in the CPS<10 contingency, not because the data are strong.
primary_concerns: TNT BRCA-mut readout is a pre-specified but n=43 subgroup; the HR 0.59 must be cited with its wide CI, not dressed up as a primary-endpoint hit.
No registrational 1L OS data for carboplatin/gemcitabine specifically in PD-L1-low BRCA1-mut mTNBC; the regimen rests on TNT class evidence plus post-marketing use.
Grade >=3 neutropenia 30-40% and thrombocytopenia ~15% are well-characterized and managed with standard supportive-care algorithms.

notes: Re-run posture after the 14 new on-axis trials and the DDR evidence append: my ranking does not move. I rank on registered primary-endpoint hits, replication, and RoB 2 grade, and the new material is almost entirely 2L+ single-arm or abstract-only, so it cannot outrank the replicated PARP RCTs for a treatment-naive patient. Where the new evidence does matter is in policing what the other personas will do with it. Specific holds I will raise in round 2: (1) saruparib PETRA (48.4% breast ORR, n=31 at 60 mg) and HS-10502 are PARP1-selective abstracts with mixed HR+/TNBC subsets, null PMIDs, and no per-term AE tables; strong-looking single-arm ORR, but it does not replace a randomized PARP1/2 readout and reads as cross-subtype class precedent, not a TNBC estimate. (2) ART6043, novobiocin, SYN818 are three POLθ programs on the BRCA1 axis with essentially no clinical data; ART6043 has FDA Fast Track and a randomized POLKA trial coming, which is the right way to test it, but today it is one confirmed PR across 42 combination patients from an ESMO press summary. (3) DAT-2645 PARG has zero clinical data of its own; the IDE161 class precedent is cross-tumor (endometrial/ovarian, ER+ breast), press-release-level, not TNBC. (4) RLY-2608 and tersolisib (STX-478) are mutant-selective PI3Kalpha agents evidenced only in PIK3CA-mutant HR+/HER2- populations with a fulvestrant partner that does not exist in TNBC; cross-tumor extrapolation onto her PIK3CA feature, which is itself ngs_pending on hotspot status. CAPItello-290 already reads as phase 3 negative in TNBC including the PIK3CA/AKT/PTEN-altered stratum, which is direct RCT evidence against off-label PI3K/AKT-pathway targeting here. (5) CX-5461 is published (IND.231) but BRCA1 benefit is inferred from a BRCA2/PALB2-heavy responder set, and Nat Genet 2023 flagged a mutagenicity concern worth reading before anyone leans on it. Carried caveats unchanged: TIL 3+ needs ITWG re-scoring before any TIL-anchored argument (target_validation stromal-tils-rescore-itwg); TMB 14 should be locked to F1CDx before it gates anything (tmb-panel-assay-confirmation); NRG-BR002 was negative for off-trial SBRT consolidation (HR ~1.31), so routine liver-lesion ablation off a registered protocol is not supported; E2108 shows no OS benefit from resecting the intact primary.

picks.rationale: This is where the guidelines are least ambivalent: NCCN Breast v4.2025 lists olaparib and talazoparib as category 1 for gBRCA1/2 HER2-negative metastatic disease, and ESMO gives single-agent olaparib a class I recommendation in the same setting. OlympiAD (PFS HR 0.58) and EMBRACA (PFS HR 0.54) are both low-risk-of-bias phase 3 RCTs, so this is high-level evidence with uniform consensus rather than a subgroup signal. Between the two I lean olaparib on tolerability — talazoparib carries roughly grade 3+ anemia 39% vs olaparib's 16%. The whole category-1 claim rides on the germline-vs-somatic call, which the profile leaves open; if it resolves to somatic-only, the FDA breast label and the NCCN category-1 statement both fall away and this drops to off-label.
primary_concerns: Category-1 status is germline-gated. The breast label for both drugs is germline-BRCA; a somatic-only BRCA1 call moves this off-guideline (the somatic talazoparib data is NCT03990896, single-arm n=13, not a guideline basis).
Guideline endorsement is for single-agent PARP as a line of therapy, not as the answer to de novo oligometastatic curative-intent framing — the guidelines assume incurable metastatic disease.
Baseline ctDNA before any PARP exposure is worth having, since BRCA1 reversion is the dominant acquired-resistance route later.

picks.rationale: For 1L metastatic TNBC with PD-L1 CPS >=10 by 22C3, this is the NCCN Breast v4.2025 category-1 / preferred regimen and an ESMO class I recommendation, anchored on KEYNOTE-355 (PFS HR 0.65, final OS HR 0.73 in CPS >=10). The TIL-3+ / TMB-14 phenotype sits in the subgroup that does best, so the biology and the guideline point the same way. The catch is that the label is CPS-gated and her PD-L1 is still pending; if CPS returns <10 the regimen is off-label and the guideline-aligned move shifts toward the PD-L1-low pathway. A gemcitabine/carboplatin partner also folds in the platinum her BRCA1 status argues for, which is why I would favor that backbone over a taxane alone.
primary_concerns: Entirely gated on PD-L1 CPS >=10 by 22C3; the case has CPS pending, and primary-vs-liver-met PD-L1 discordance runs 20-30%, so score the breast primary.
TMB-14 and TIL-3+ are favorable but do not substitute for CPS in the label — the guideline endorsement is CPS-anchored, not TMB- or TIL-anchored.
Sequencing against PARP is unsettled; guidelines endorse both but do not tell you which comes first in a gBRCA CPS-high patient.

picks.rationale: NCCN and ESMO both endorse platinum as a preferred cytotoxic in gBRCA and in TNBC generally, and TNT gives the cleanest rationale specific to this patient: in the BRCA-mutant subset carboplatin doubled ORR over docetaxel (68% vs 33%, interaction p=0.01) with a PFS HR of 0.44. It is rarely the standalone answer, but it is the guideline-endorsed chemotherapy partner that threads through the CPS-high regimen (as gem/carbo + pembrolizumab) and gives a platinum induction that a later PARP or PARP+IO maintenance can build on. BrighTNess and CALGB 40603 both show the platinum, not the added PARP, drives the depth of response, which is why I weight carboplatin over veliparib-type combinations. Cross-society convergence here is strong; the evidence tier is 1b.
primary_concerns: Not a monotherapy endgame — it functions as the backbone/induction, so the ranking reflects its role in the regimen rather than a standalone recommendation.
Myelosuppression stacks if combined with gem/carbo + pembrolizumab (KEYNOTE-355 grade 3+ neutropenia ~41%); the guideline assumes the marrow reserve to support it.
TNT enrolled pretreated patients; extrapolating the BRCA-mut carboplatin advantage to the 1L de novo setting is reasonable but is an extrapolation the guideline makes implicitly, not explicitly.

picks.intervention_label: Trial enrollment — next-generation DDR agent (PARP1-selective, POLθ, or mutant-selective PI3Kα)
picks.rationale: The profile is unusually trial-eligible (BRCA1, PIK3CA, PTEN loss, MYC/IRS2, TMB-14, TIL-rich, young, single-site) and preferences.json sets prefers_trials true, so for the investigational agents the guideline-aligned route is enrollment, not off-label prescribing. The strongest class signal is PARP1-selective: saruparib in the PETRA breast subset gave ORR 48.4% (80% CI 35.7-61.3) with less hematologic toxicity than approved PARP1/2 inhibitors, which is the cleanest precedent for the recruiting HS-10502 HRR-mutant breast cohort (NCT05740956). The POLθ programs (ART6043, with FDA Fast Track in gBRCA breast) and mutant-selective PI3Kalpha agents (RLY-2608, tersolisib) are earlier but on-axis. None of these is guideline-endorsed as therapy yet — they belong in the dossier as trial options, mostly after a first-line PARP/platinum/IO, and PIK3CA-axis entry is gated on hotspot confirmation.
primary_concerns: All investigational or off-label — no NCCN/ESMO category applies; the honest framing is trial-enrollment, not standard therapy.
Most of these gates require prior standard-of-care or PARP exposure, so they sit after 1L, not at presentation.
PI3Kalpha-axis eligibility (RLY-2608, tersolisib) depends on resolving the PIK3CA variant to a recognized oncogenic hotspot, which is still pending; a non-hotspot call may not qualify.
Efficacy estimates for the PARP1-selective and PI3Kalpha classes come from mixed HR+/TNBC or cross-tumor abstracts, not TNBC-specific peer-reviewed data.

picks.intervention_label: Pembrolizumab monotherapy on the TMB-high tumor-agnostic indication
picks.rationale: Her TMB of 14 mut/Mb clears the >=10 threshold for the tumor-agnostic pembrolizumab indication, which NCCN carries as a category 2A option and which the FDA approved off KEYNOTE-158 (ORR 29% in the TMB-H cohort). Two things keep it at rank 5 rather than higher. First, the label is restricted to patients who have progressed on a prior line with no satisfactory alternatives, and she is treatment-naive, so it does not apply in 1L. Second, breast cancer was not in the KEYNOTE-158 basket, so applying it here is cross-tumor extrapolation, and the value depends on the TMB call having been made on FoundationOne CDx (the companion diagnostic in the label). It is a defensible later-line option once she has exhausted the CPS-anchored and PARP routes, not a front-line pick.
primary_concerns: Label requires prior progression + no satisfactory alternatives; not applicable to a treatment-naive 1L patient.
Breast was not in the KEYNOTE-158 basket — this is cross-tumor extrapolation, and NCCN carries the tumor-agnostic indication at category 2A, not category 1.
Value hinges on the TMB-14 call being locked to FoundationOne CDx; a non-F1CDx call near the 10 mut/Mb cutoff should be confirmed before this gates therapy.
MSS status and any B2M/HLA class I loss would blunt expected ICI benefit despite the favorable TMB/TIL signal.

notes: Re-run over the refreshed option set (14 gate-swept trials + DDR-tier clinical rows). My ordering tracks guideline endorsement strength, not novelty: PARP (NCCN cat 1) and CPS-high pembro+chemo (NCCN cat 1) lead, both gated on pending biomarkers (germline resolution; PD-L1 CPS by 22C3). Carboplatin is the convergent backbone. The novel DDR/PI3Kalpha agents are real and on-axis but investigational — enrollment is the guideline-aligned route, and I have deliberately kept them at rank 4 rather than letting mechanistic appeal outrank category-1 standards. TMB-agnostic pembro is genuine (cat 2A) but 1L-inapplicable and cross-tumor. No veto: nothing here is contraindicated for her population. Two gating tests do real work on my ranks 1-2 and should be foregrounded: germline BRCA1 resolution and PD-L1 CPS on the breast primary.

picks.rationale: This is still the trial the preference file reads as written for, and nothing in the re-run knocks it off the top. Recruiting, 1L, randomized against the exact KEYNOTE-355 backbone she would otherwise get off-trial, gated on the pending CPS. The TROP2-ADC arm goes straight at her basal feature and the durvalumab arm cashes in the TMB-14 / TIL-3+ signal. Trial-first preference met, efficacy lean at 0.7 met by the experimental arm, and the control arm is standard of care, so the floor is bounded no matter which way she randomizes.
primary_concerns: Gated on the pending PD-L1 CPS by 22C3 >=10. If CPS returns <10 she is out of this trial and pick 1 collapses to the CPS-low ADC options (TROPION-Breast02, TroFuse-011).

Preference axes fully satisfied: trials preference honored (recruiting, on-axis), efficacy weight honored (experimental TROP2-ADC + ICI), no toxicity_vetoes to breach, no modality_constraints to breach.

picks.rationale: The registrational 1L standard if CPS returns >=10, and for this patient the carboplatin flavor does two jobs at once: the TNT data show BRCA1-mutant TNBC doubles its response rate on platinum versus taxane, so the ICI backbone and the BRCA1 axis get served by one regimen. Final OS in CPS>=10 was 23 vs 16 months, which is the efficacy-forward answer a 0.7 weight consents to. Her TIL-3+ / TMB-14 phenotype is the exact subset that pulls the largest benefit in the KEYNOTE analyses. If CPS lands under 10, this drops off and the CPS-low ADC route takes over.
primary_concerns: Same CPS-gating dependency as pick 1; the whole ICI-backbone plan rests on the pending 22C3 result.
Trials preference only partially honored: this is off-trial standard of care, honored on the trial axis mainly as TROPION-Breast05's control arm.
Efficacy/toxicity weight satisfied; no veto or modality preference to violate.

picks.intervention_label: Olaparib 300 mg PO BID (BRCA1-directed PARPi, OlympiAD label)
picks.rationale: Oral, single-agent, guideline-backed the moment the germline BRCA1 test confirms. OlympiAD and EMBRACA sit close on efficacy; talazoparib carries the heavier anemia load, so I put olaparib first because the gentler hematologic margin keeps her on drug longer and slots more cleanly around later liver-directed consolidation. The preference file sets no modality constraint, so oral is my advocacy tilt for a 42-year-old with a curative framing, not a rule I am reading in. As a 1L single agent it honors the efficacy lean without maximizing it, which is why it sits behind the ICI backbone rather than ahead of it.
primary_concerns: Eligibility gated on germline BRCA1 resolution. A somatic-only call takes her off the OlympiAD/EMBRACA label and onto the somatic-BRCA Stanford talazoparib trial (NCT03990896) instead, which is still on-axis and preference-compatible.
Single-agent PARPi is less aggressive than ICI+chemo in 1L; fits the 0.7 weight but does not push it. Reads best as a bridge or as the post-induction maintenance answer.
No toxicity_veto and no modality_constraint in the file, so nothing here breaches a stated preference; the oral-preference framing is advocate judgment, flagged as such.

picks.intervention_label: Olaparib + ceralasertib (ATR inhibitor) on the recruiting germline-BRCA arm (NCT04090567)
picks.rationale: New this re-run and it earns a spot. The MD Anderson trial pairs olaparib with ceralasertib in germline-BRCA HER2-negative advanced breast cancer and is recruiting, so the ATR combination VIOLETTE could only test in a now-closed study has a live home. Her BRCA1 plus TP53 is the replication-stress genotype the mechanism was built for, and plasmaMATCH Cohort E is the honest anchor: 17% ORR in pretreated mTNBC with responses landing in HRR-wildtype tumors too, not just BRCA carriers. I am not overselling it. VIOLETTE was negative over olaparib alone and the combination adds anemia and hypertension, so I rank this below single-agent olaparib and reserve it for after her first line, where the trials preference and the DDR axis both point to it.
primary_concerns: VIOLETTE showed the combination did not beat olaparib monotherapy, and the added anemia/hypertension is real; this is earlier-evidence DDR territory, not a settled win, and I am flagging that honestly per the user's stated trial-forward but efficacy-weighted lens.
Germline-gated like pick 3, and positioned 2L+, so it is a later-line trial slot rather than a 1L option.
Trials preference strongly honored (recruiting, on-axis for BRCA1+TP53); no veto or modality breach.

picks.intervention_label: SBRT to solitary liver lesion as consolidation on MSK SABR trial (NCT05534438) after systemic response
picks.rationale: The preference file's curative-intent framing is explicit, and a solitary 1.5 cm hepatic lesion is the most consolidatable disease this patient will ever present with. I keep this on the list because the free-text asks me to, but I carry the counter-evidence with it: NRG-BR002's phase IIR PFS readout favored systemic therapy alone, and E2108 found no OS benefit from local therapy of the intact primary in de novo M1. The MSK protocol enrolls de novo oligometastatic disease specifically and lets her get SBRT under trial once a 12-week scan confirms the breast and axilla are controlled. It layers on the systemic backbone from picks 1-2, never replaces it.
primary_concerns: NRG-BR002 phase IIR PFS was negative for consolidation and E2108 was negative for OS; the curative-intent rationale rests on biology selection of a single small lesion, not a positive randomized signal, and the user should hear that plainly.
Consolidation, not systemic therapy; only defensible layered on top of the picks above after documented response.
Trials preference satisfied via the MSK slot; the curative framing in free_text is what brings this onto a 1L ranking at all.

picks.intervention_label: PARP1-selective inhibitor (HS-10502 on NCT05740956; saruparib/PETRA as class precedent)
picks.rationale: Worth surfacing because it answers a tolerability question the preference file cares about even without a formal veto. PARP1-selective agents are designed to spare the anemia and thrombocytopenia that cap olaparib and talazoparib, and the saruparib PETRA breast subset read out at 48% ORR with a wide therapeutic index. HS-10502 has a dedicated HRR-mutant HER2-negative breast cohort that her BRCA1 status matches directly and is recruiting. I rank it last because HS-10502's own efficacy is unpublished and the class evidence is conference-level and cross-subtype, but for a young patient facing years of DDR-axis therapy the toxicity-sparing angle is exactly the kind of preference-aligned upside I am here to raise.
primary_concerns: HS-10502 has no published efficacy or safety readout; the 48% ORR belongs to saruparib (PETRA, abstract-level) and mixes HR+ and TNBC, so it is class precedent, not a TNBC-specific estimate.
Positioned 2L+ (prior standard therapy required), so a later-line trial slot; germline-vs-somatic status still shapes the sequencing.
Trials preference honored; the toxicity-sparing rationale aligns with the efficacy-leaning-but-liveable spirit of the 0.7 weight even though no toxicity_veto is set.

notes: Fresh round-1 over the full current option set after the 14-trial re-run. The preference file is thin on explicit constraints (no toxicity_vetoes, no modality_constraints, efficacy weight 0.7, prefers_trials true, curative-intent free_text), so the ranking is driven by: trials-first (pushes recruiting on-axis options up), efficacy lean 0.7 (favors the ICI/ADC backbone over single-agent PARPi in 1L), and the curative framing (brings SBRT consolidation onto a 1L list). Picks 1-2 are CPS-gated and swap to TROPION-Breast02/TroFuse-011 if 22C3 returns <10. Picks 3-4 are germline-gated; a somatic-only BRCA1 shifts pick 3 to the Stanford talazoparib trial (NCT03990896) and keeps pick 4 open (NCT04090567 accepts germline; the somatic route runs through the DFCI axatilimab+olaparib study NCT06488378). New evidence honestly weighted: olaparib+ceralasertib now has real but modest TNBC data (plasmaMATCH Cohort E, negative VIOLETTE comparison) and the PARP1-selective class is promising but abstract-level. I did not surface capivasertib despite her PIK3CA/PTEN axis because CAPItello-290 read out negative in TNBC including the AKT-altered stratum, and I did not lead with a POLθ or PARG trial because those are washout-gated and treatment-naive-incompatible right now. No preference is violated by any pick; where a pick is earlier-evidence I said so rather than dressing it up.
